pharm: Inhibits phosphodiesterase III, suppressing cAMP degradation in platelets and vascular smooth muscle, which reversibly inhibits platelet aggregation and produces vasodilation
tags: BOXED WARNING: contraindicated in heart failure of any severity
quick: 100 mg twice daily; reduce to 50 mg twice daily with CYP3A4 or CYP2C19 inhibitors
Take at least 30 minutes before or 2 hours after breakfast and dinner (a high-fat meal increases absorption)
Category C; teratogenic in animals; no adequate human studies
Discontinue nursing or discontinue the drug (found in rat milk)
No adjustment needed; dialysis patients not studied (not efficiently dialyzable)
No adjustment in mild; not studied in moderate-severe (no dosing recommendation)
No specific interaction; excess may add to GI/bleeding risk
Platelet and white blood cell counts; cardiac symptoms/new murmur; heart rate
summary: Cilostazol is an oral phosphodiesterase-3 inhibitor used to reduce the symptoms of intermittent claudication, demonstrated by increased walking distance. It inhibits platelet aggregation and dilates blood vessels. It carries a BOXED WARNING that it is contraindicated in patients with heart failure of any severity, because drugs sharing this PDE-3 inhibitory effect have decreased survival in patients with class III-IV heart failure. Benefit may take 2-12 weeks to appear; discontinue if symptoms are not improved after 3 months.
indications: Reduction of the symptoms of intermittent claudication, as demonstrated by an increased walking distance

dosage.t: Response may begin at 2-4 weeks; up to 12 weeks may be needed for benefit; discontinue if no improvement after 3 months
dosage.n: Take at least 30 minutes before or 2 hours after breakfast and dinner

dosage.r: Coadministered with strong/moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole, itraconazole, erythromycin, diltiazem) or CYP2C19 inhibitors (e.g. ticlopidine, fluconazole, omeprazole)
dosage.n: Dose reduction accounts for increased cilostazol exposure

admin: Give 100 mg twice daily at least 30 minutes before or 2 hours after breakfast and dinner
Reduce to 50 mg twice daily when given with strong/moderate CYP3A4 or CYP2C19 inhibitors
Avoid taking with food and with grapefruit juice (alters absorption)
Do not use in any patient with heart failure of any severity (see BOXED WARNING)
Discontinue if symptoms of claudication are not improved after 3 months
moa: Cilostazol and several of its metabolites inhibit phosphodiesterase III and suppress cAMP degradation, raising cAMP in platelets and blood vessels. This reversibly inhibits platelet aggregation induced by thrombin, ADP, collagen, arachidonic acid, epinephrine, and shear stress, and produces vasodilation (with greater dilation of femoral than vertebral, carotid, or mesenteric beds). As a PDE-3 inhibitor it also increases heart rate, myocardial contractility, and AV conduction.

absolute: Heart failure of any severity (PDE-3 inhibitors have decreased survival in class III-IV heart failure)
Hypersensitivity to cilostazol or any component (e.g. anaphylaxis, angioedema)
relative: History of ischemic heart disease (risk of angina exacerbation or MI from increased heart rate)
Sigmoid-shaped interventricular septum (left ventricular outflow tract obstruction reported)
Hemostatic disorders or active pathologic bleeding (avoid use)
monitor: Platelet and white blood cell counts (risk of thrombocytopenia/leukopenia progressing to agranulocytosis)
New systolic murmur or cardiac symptoms after starting therapy

preg: Pregnancy Category C. Cilostazol was teratogenic in rats at doses greater than about 5 times the human MRHD on a body-surface-area basis, causing decreased fetal weights and increased cardiovascular, renal, and skeletal anomalies (including ventricular septal defect, aortic arch and subclavian artery abnormalities, renal pelvic dilation, extra rib, and retarded ossification); ventricular septal defect and retarded ossification also occurred at 150 mg/kg/day (about 5 times the MRHD on an exposure basis). Rabbit studies showed retarded sternal ossification, and dosing in late pregnancy/lactation increased stillbirths and decreased birth weights. There are no adequate, well-controlled studies in pregnant women.
lact: Transfer of cilostazol into milk has been reported in rats. Because many drugs are excreted in human milk and because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in nursing infants, either discontinue nursing or discontinue cilostazol, taking into account the importance of the drug to the mother.
renal: No dose adjustment is required in renal impairment. Total pharmacologic activity of cilostazol and its metabolites was similar in mild-to-moderate renal impairment versus healthy subjects; severe impairment raises metabolite levels and alters parent protein binding but expected activity appears little changed. Dialysis patients have not been studied, but cilostazol is unlikely to be efficiently removed by dialysis given its high (95-98%) protein binding.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is required in mild hepatic impairment, where pharmacokinetics were similar to healthy subjects. Patients with moderate or severe hepatic impairment have not been studied and dosing recommendations cannot be provided.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole, itraconazole, voriconazole, clarithromycin, ritonavir, saquinavir, nefazodone) - markedly increase exposure; reduce dose to 50 mg twice daily
CYP2C19 inhibitors (e.g. omeprazole, ticlopidine, fluconazole) - increase active metabolite exposure; reduce dose to 50 mg twice daily
moderate: Moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. erythromycin and other macrolides, diltiazem) - increase exposure; reduce dose to 50 mg twice daily
Aspirin - additive ex vivo inhibition of platelet aggregation (no clinically significant change in PT/aPTT/bleeding time short-term)
Lovastatin - cilostazol raises lovastatin AUC ~70% (not expected to be clinically significant)
minor: Clopidogrel - no significant change in cilostazol steady-state levels
Warfarin - cilostazol did not inhibit single-dose warfarin pharmacology
Quinidine - no change in cilostazol pharmacokinetics
interactions.food: Take at least 30 minutes before or 2 hours after meals; a high-fat meal raises Cmax by ~90% and AUC by ~25%; grapefruit juice raises Cmax by ~50%
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction described; excess alcohol may add to GI or bleeding risk
interactions.diagnostics: After 12 weeks, cilostazol 100 mg twice daily reduced triglycerides ~15% and raised HDL-cholesterol ~10%

common: Dizziness, pharyngitis, peripheral edema, rhinitis, dyspepsia, abdominal pain, tachycardia
serious: Thrombocytopenia or leukopenia progressing to agranulocytosis
Myocardial infarction, angina pectoris, heart failure
Left ventricular outflow tract obstruction (in sigmoid septum)
Torsade de pointes / QTc prolongation in patients with cardiac disorders
rare: Aplastic anemia, pancytopenia, granulocytopenia, bleeding tendency
Intracranial/cerebral hemorrhage, cerebrovascular accident, subdural/extradural hematoma
Stevens-Johnson syndrome, hepatic dysfunction/jaundice, interstitial pneumonia, pulmonary hemorrhage
emergency: Torsade de pointes or symptomatic arrhythmia

monitoring: Platelet and white blood cell counts periodically (agranulocytosis is reversible if drug stopped promptly)
New systolic murmur or cardiac symptoms (LV outflow tract obstruction)
Heart rate and symptoms of angina or arrhythmia
Walking distance / symptom response at 3 months - discontinue if no improvement
counsel: Take cilostazol at least 30 minutes before or 2 hours after food, twice daily
Tell your doctor before starting any CYP3A4 or CYP2C19 inhibitor (such as omeprazole), as the dose may need to be lowered
Benefit on claudication symptoms is not immediate - you may notice improvement in 2-4 weeks, but it can take up to 12 weeks; the drug will be stopped if symptoms have not improved after 3 months
This drug must NOT be used if you have any degree of heart failure - tell your doctor about any heart condition
Report fever, signs of infection, easy bruising or bleeding, a fast or pounding heartbeat, or chest pain
Avoid grapefruit juice, which can raise drug levels
pk: Platelet aggregation inhibition seen as early as 3 hours post-dose; symptom benefit may take 2-12 weeks
Dose-proportional kinetics; steady state reached within a few days (~2-fold accumulation)
Cilostazol and its active metabolites have apparent elimination half-lives of about 11 to 13 hours
Single-dose platelet effect lasts up to 12 hours; after chronic dosing the effect subsides by 48 h and returns to baseline by 96 h with no rebound
Store at 25 C (77 F); excursions permitted 15-30 C (59-86 F)
pearls: BOXED WARNING: contraindicated in heart failure of ANY severity - PDE-3 inhibitors have decreased survival versus placebo in class III-IV heart failure
Indicated only to reduce intermittent claudication symptoms (increase walking distance), not for survival or limb outcomes
Reduce to 50 mg twice daily with CYP3A4 or CYP2C19 inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole, erythromycin, diltiazem, omeprazole)
Take on an empty stomach (>=30 min before or 2 h after meals); high-fat meals and grapefruit juice raise absorption
Increases heart rate by ~5-7 bpm - caution with ischemic heart disease; watch for angina or MI
Monitor CBC - thrombocytopenia/leukopenia can progress to agranulocytosis (reversible if stopped promptly)
Also lowers triglycerides (~15%) and raises HDL (~10%) over 12 weeks
Discontinue if no symptom improvement after 3 months
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember, observing the timing relative to meals. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your usual twice-daily schedule. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: Human data are limited. Acute overdose is expected to cause exaggerated pharmacologic effects: severe headache, diarrhea, hypotension, tachycardia, and possibly cardiac arrhythmias. Observe the patient carefully and give supportive treatment. Because cilostazol is highly protein-bound, it is unlikely to be efficiently removed by hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis.
